questions.stem: A charge $Q$ is placed at each of the opposite corners of a square. A charge $q$ is placed at each of the other two corners. If the net electrical force on $Q$ is zero, then $Q/q$ equals:
questions.solution:
It is given that $\vec{F}_A + \vec{F}_B + \vec{F}_D = 0$, where $\vec{F}_A, \vec{F}_B$ and $\vec{F}_D$ are the forces applied by charges placed at A, B and D on the charge placed at C.

$\Rightarrow \vec{F}_B + \vec{F}_D = -\vec{F}_A$

$\left|\vec{F}_B + \vec{F}_D\right| = \sqrt{2}\dfrac{KqQ}{a^2}$, $\quad \left|\vec{F}_A\right| = \dfrac{KQ^2}{2a^2}$

$$\therefore \sqrt{2}\frac{KqQ}{a^2} = -\frac{KQ^2}{2a^2} \Rightarrow \frac{Q}{q} = -2\sqrt{2}$$

questions.stem: A U-shaped tube contains a liquid of density $\rho$ and it is rotated about the left dotted line as shown in the figure. Find the difference in the levels of liquid column.
questions.solution:
For the horizontal liquid column of length $L$ rotating about the left arm, the pressure difference needed to provide centripetal force is

$$\Delta P = \int_0^L \rho\omega^2 x\,dx = \frac{\rho\omega^2L^2}{2}$$

This is supplied by the level difference: $\rho g H = \dfrac{\rho\omega^2L^2}{2} \Rightarrow H = \dfrac{\omega^2L^2}{2g}$

questions.stem: The angle of dip at a place is $37^\circ$ and the vertical component of the earth's magnetic field is $6 \times 10^{-5}$ T. The earth's magnetic field at this place is ($\tan 37^\circ = \frac{3}{4}$)
questions.solution: $B_V = B\sin\delta \Rightarrow B = \dfrac{B_V}{\sin 37^\circ} = \dfrac{6\times10^{-5}}{3/5} = 10^{-4}\ \text{T}$

questions.stem: A body of weight $2$ kg is suspended as shown in the figure. The tension $T_1$ in the horizontal string (in kgwt) is
questions.solution:
Let $T$ be the tension in the inclined string making $30^\circ$ with the ceiling.

Vertical: $T\sin30^\circ = 2 \Rightarrow T = 4$ kgwt

Horizontal: $T_1 = T\cos30^\circ = 4\times\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2\sqrt{3}$ kgwt

questions.stem: A solenoid is $2$ m long and $3$ cm in diameter. It has $5$ layers of winding of $1000$ turns each and carries a current of $5$ A. What is the magnetic field at its centre? Use the standard value of $\mu_0$.
questions.solution:
$n = \dfrac{5\times1000}{2} = 2500\ \text{m}^{-1}$

$B = \mu_0 nI = 4\pi\times10^{-7}\times2500\times5 = 1.57\times10^{-2}\ \text{T}$

questions.stem: Four massless springs with force constants $2k$, $2k$, $k$ and $2k$ respectively are connected to a mass $M$ kept on a frictionless plane as shown in figure. If the mass $M$ is displaced in the horizontal direction, then the frequency of the system is?
questions.solution:
The equivalent system is a spring $k$ (two $2k$ in series) on the left and $3k$ ($k$ and $2k$ in parallel) on the right.

The equivalent force constant: $k_e = k + 3k = 4k$

$$\omega = \sqrt{\frac{k_e}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{4k}{m}} = 2\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}, \quad f = \frac{\omega}{2\pi} = \frac{1}{\pi}\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$$

questions.stem: A gun fires two bullets at $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$ with horizontal. The bullets strike at some horizontal distance. The ratio of maximum height for the two bullets is in the ratio of
questions.solution:
Both bullets have the same range (complementary angles). $H = \dfrac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$

$$\frac{H_1}{H_2} = \frac{\sin^2 60^\circ}{\sin^2 30^\circ} = \frac{3/4}{1/4} = 3:1$$

questions.stem: A proton moving with a velocity $3 \times 10^5$ m/s enters a magnetic field of $0.3$ tesla at an angle of $30^\circ$ with the field. The radius of curvature of its path will be ($e/m$ for proton $= 10^8$ C/kg)

questions.stem: The electric potential V is given as a function of distance $x$ (metre) by $V = 5x^2 + 10x - 4$ volt. Value of electric field at $x = 1$ m is

Consider the optical system shown in Fig. The point source of light $S$ is having wavelength equal to $\lambda$. The light is reaching screen only after reflection. For point $\mathbf{P}$ to be second maxima, the value of $\lambda$ would be ($D \gg d$ and $d \gg \lambda$)
questions.solution:
The images $S_1$ and $S_2$ of $S$ in the two mirrors are separated by $8d$, and $P$ is at height $3d$ above the central maxima $O$.

At P, $\Delta x = \dfrac{(8d)\times3d}{D}$

For 2nd maxima, $\Delta x = 2\lambda$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{24d^2}{D} = 2\lambda \Rightarrow \lambda = \dfrac{12d^2}{D}$

questions.stem: The compressibility of water is $4 \times 10^{-5}$ per unit atmospheric pressure. The decrease in volume of $100\ \text{cm}^3$ of water under a pressure of $100$ atmosphere will be
questions.solution:
Compressibility $= \dfrac{1}{B} = \dfrac{\Delta V/V}{P}$

Here, $P = 100$ atm, compressibility $= 4\times10^{-5}$ and $V = 100\ \text{cm}^3$

Hence, $\Delta V = 4\times10^{-5}\times100\times100 = 0.4\ \text{cm}^3$

questions.stem: A plane electromagnetic wave is incident on a plane surface of area A, normally and is perfectly reflected. If energy $E$ strikes the surface in time $t$ then force exerted on the surface is ($c$ = speed of light)
questions.solution:
Incident momentum, $p = \dfrac{E}{c}$

For perfectly reflecting surface with normal incidence

$\Delta p = 2p = \dfrac{2E}{c}$; $\quad F = \dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{2E}{ct}$

questions.stem: A point particle is held on the axis of a ring of mass $m$ and radius $r$ at a distance $r$ from its centre $C$. When released, it reaches $C$ under the gravitational attraction of the ring. Its speed at $C$ will be
questions.solution:
Let $M$ be the mass of the particle. $E_{initial} = E_{final}$

$$-\frac{GMm}{\sqrt{2}r} + 0 = -\frac{GMm}{r} + \frac{1}{2}MV^2$$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2}V^2 = \dfrac{Gm}{r}\left[1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]$ or, $V = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Gm}{r}\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}$

questions.stem: Electrons are accelerated through a potential difference $V$ and protons are accelerated through a potential difference $4V$. The de-Broglie wavelengths are $\lambda_e$ and $\lambda_p$ for electrons and protons respectively. The ratio of $\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p}$ is given by: (given $m_e$ is mass of electron and $m_p$ is mass of proton).
questions.solution:
$E_{electron} = q_eV$ and $E_{proton} = q_p 4V$

de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$

$\lambda_e = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_eeV}}$ and $\lambda_p = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m_pe4V}}$ $\quad(\because q_e = q_p)$

$$\therefore \frac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p} = 2\sqrt{\frac{m_p}{m_e}}$$

questions.stem: An ideal gas at atmospheric pressure is adiabatically compressed so that its density becomes $32$ times of its initial value. If the final pressure of gas is $128$ atmospheres, the value of '$\gamma$' of the gas is:
questions.solution:
Volume $V = \dfrac{m}{d}$ and using $PV^\gamma$ = constant

$\dfrac{P'}{P} = \left(\dfrac{V}{V'}\right)^\gamma = \left(\dfrac{d'}{d}\right)^\gamma$

or $128 = (32)^\gamma \Rightarrow 2^7 = 2^{5\gamma}$

$\therefore \gamma = \dfrac{7}{5} = 1.4$

questions.stem: Monochromatic light of wavelength $667$ nm is produced by a helium neon laser. The power emitted is $9$ mW. The number of photons arriving per sec on the average at a target irradiated by this beam is:

$$N = \frac{9\times10^{-3}\times667\times10^{-9}}{6.6\times10^{-34}\times3\times10^8} = 3\times10^{16}/\text{sec}$$

questions.stem: The frequency of whistle of an engine appears to be $\left(\dfrac{4}{5}\right)^{\text{th}}$ of initial frequency when it crosses a stationary observer. If the velocity of sound is $330$ m/s, then the speed of engine will be
questions.solution:
$n' = \dfrac{nv}{v - v_s}$ ....(1) $\quad n'' = \dfrac{nv}{v + v_s}$ ....(2)

From (1) and (2), $\dfrac{n'}{n''} = \dfrac{v + v_s}{v - v_s}$ ....(3)

According to question, $\dfrac{n'}{n''} = \dfrac{5}{4}$, $v = 330$ m/s

$\dfrac{5}{4} = \dfrac{330 + v_s}{330 - v_s} \Rightarrow 9v_s = 330$

$\therefore v_s = 36.6$ m/s

questions.stem: A moving coil galvanometer has resistance of $10\,\Omega$ and full scale deflection of $0.01$ A. It can be converted into voltmeter of $10$ V full scale by connecting into resistance of
questions.solution:
Let $G$ be resistance of galvanometer and $i_g$ the current through it. Let $V$ be maximum potential difference, then from Ohm's law

$i_g = \dfrac{V}{G + R} \Rightarrow R = \dfrac{V}{i_g} - G$

Given, $G = 10\,\Omega$, $i_g = 0.01$ A, $V = 10$ volt

$\therefore R = \dfrac{10}{0.01} - 10 = 990\,\Omega$

Thus, on connecting a resistance $R$ of $990\,\Omega$ in series with the galvanometer, it will become a voltmeter of range zero to 10 V.

questions.stem: In a simple pendulum of length $l$ the bob is pulled aside from its equilibrium position through an angle $\theta$ and then released. The bob passes through the equilibrium position with speed
questions.solution:
If $l$ is length of pendulum and $\theta$ be angular amplitude then from principle of conservation of energy

$0 + mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 + 0$

$\Rightarrow v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2gl(1-\cos\theta)}$

questions.stem: A zener diode of voltage $V_Z (= 6\ \text{V})$ is used to maintain a constant voltage across a load resistance $R_L (= 1000\,\Omega)$ by using a series resistance $R_s (= 100\,\Omega)$. If the e.m.f. of source is $E (= 9\ \text{V})$, what is the power being dissipated in Zener diode?
questions.solution:
Here, $E = 9$ V; $V_Z = 6$ V; $R_L = 1000\,\Omega$ and $R_s = 100\,\Omega$

Potential drop across series resistor: $V = E - V_Z = 9 - 6 = 3$ V

Current through series resistance: $I = \dfrac{3}{100} = 0.03$ A

Current through load resistance: $I_L = \dfrac{V_Z}{R_L} = \dfrac{6}{1000} = 0.006$ A

Current through Zener diode: $I_Z = I - I_L = 0.03 - 0.006 = 0.024$ A

Power dissipated in Zener diode: $P_Z = V_ZI_Z = 6\times0.024 = 0.144$ W

questions.stem: A ball of mass $0.2$ kg is thrown vertically upwards by applying a force by hand. If the hand moves $0.2$ m while applying the force and the ball goes upto $2$ m height further, find the magnitude of the force. (Consider $g = 10\ \text{m/s}^2$).
questions.solution:
Let the velocity of the ball just when it leaves the hand be $u$. Applying $v^2 - u^2 = 2as$ for the upward journey

$\Rightarrow -u^2 = 2(-10)\times2 \Rightarrow u^2 = 40$

When the ball is in the hands of the thrower: $40 - 0 = 2(a)(0.2) \Rightarrow a = 100\ \text{m/s}^2$

$\therefore F_{net} = ma = 0.2\times100 = 20$ N

$\Rightarrow N - mg = 20 \Rightarrow N = 20 + 2 = 22$ N

questions.stem: A wire of a certain material is stretched slowly by ten per cent. Its new resistance and specific resistance become respectively:
questions.solution:
$R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}$. Volume $V = lA$ remains constant.

New length $l' = 1.1\,l$, so new area $A' = \dfrac{A}{1.1}$

$$R' = \rho\frac{1.1\,l}{A/1.1} = 1.21\,\rho\frac{l}{A} = 1.21R$$

So, the resistance increases 1.21 times, while resistivity (a material property) remains the same.

questions.stem: Three specimens A, B, C of same radioactive element have activities $1$ microcurie, $1$ rutherford and $1$ becquerel respectively. Which specimen has maximum mass?
questions.solution:
1 becquerel $= 1$ dis/s

1 rutherford $= 10^6$ dis/s

1 microcurie $= 3.7\times10^{4}$ dis/s

Since activity $\propto$ number of nuclei (mass) for the same element, B (1 rutherford) has the maximum mass.

questions.stem: Suppose the law of gravitational attraction suddenly changes and becomes an inverse cube law i.e. $F \propto \dfrac{1}{r^3}$, but still remaining a central force. Then

options.text: Kepler's law of area still holds
Kepler's law of period still holds
Kepler's law of area and period still holds
neither the law of area, nor the law of period still holds

questions.solution:
According to Kepler's law of area

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \dfrac{L}{2m}$

For central forces, torque $= 0$, $\therefore L$ = constant

$\therefore \dfrac{dA}{dt}$ = constant. (The law of periods depends on the inverse-square form and no longer holds.)

questions.stem: Green light of wavelength $5460\,\text{Å}$ is incident on an air-glass interface. If the refractive index of glass is $1.5$, the wavelength of light in glass would be ($c = 3\times10^8\ \text{ms}^{-1}$)

questions.stem: An alternating voltage $V = V_0\sin\omega t$ is applied across a circuit. As a result, a current $I = I_0\sin\left(\omega t - \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ flows in it. The power consumed per cycle is
questions.solution:
The phase angle between voltage V and current I is $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Therefore, power factor $\cos\phi = \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 0$.

Hence the power consumed is zero.

questions.stem: A balloon is rising vertically up with a velocity of $29\ \text{ms}^{-1}$. A stone is dropped from it and it reaches the ground in $10$ seconds. The height of the balloon when the stone was dropped from it, was ($g = 9.8\ \text{ms}^{-2}$)

For stone dropped from rising balloon of velocity 29 m/s, $u = -29$ m/s, $t = 10$ sec.

$\therefore h = -29\times10 + \dfrac{1}{2}\times9.8\times100 = -290 + 490 = 200$ m.

questions.stem: A metal disc of radius $100$ cm is rotated at a constant angular speed of $60$ rad/s in a plane at right angles to an external field of magnetic induction $0.05\ \text{Wb/m}^2$. The emf induced between the centre and a point on the rim will be

$\omega = 60$ rad/s, $B = 0.05\ \text{Wb/m}^2$, $R = 1$ m

$e = \dfrac{1}{2}\times60\times0.05\times1^2 = 1.5$ V

questions.stem: In a given network the equivalent capacitance between A and B is ($C_1 = C_4 = 1\,\mu\text{F}$, $C_2 = C_3 = 2\,\mu\text{F}$):

Redrawing the network, $C_1$, $C_4$ and the series combination of $C_3$ and $C_2$ are in parallel between A and B:

questions.stem: A spherical drop of radius $R$ is divided into eight equal droplets. If surface tension is $T$, then the work done in this process is
questions.solution:
Volume of 8 small droplets = Volume of 1 big drop

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\times8 = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{R}{2}$

Work done = (Change in area) $\times$ surface tension

$$= (4\pi r^2\times8 - 4\pi R^2)T = \left(4\pi\frac{R^2}{4}\times8 - 4\pi R^2\right)T = 4\pi R^2T$$

questions.stem: A round disc of moment of inertia $I_2$ about its axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through its centre is placed over another disc of moment of inertia $I_1$ rotating with an angular velocity $\omega$ about the same axis. questions.stem: Three particles, each of mass $m$ grams are situated at the vertices of an equilateral triangle $ABC$ of side $l$ cm (as shown in the figure). The moment of inertia of the system about a line $AX$ perpendicular to $AB$ and in the plane of $ABC$ in g-cm$^2$ units will be:

questions.stem:
In the reaction:

$\text{CH}_3-\underset{\text{CH}_3}{\text{CH}}-\text{CH}_2-\text{O}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3 + \text{HI} \xrightarrow{\text{Heated}}$

Which of the following compounds will be formed?

questions.stem: $\text{PCl}_5$ is dissociating $50\%$ at $250^\circ$C at a total pressure of $P$ atm. If equilibrium constant is $K_p$, then which of the following relation is numerically correct -
questions.solution:
$\text{PCl}_5 \rightarrow \text{PCl}_3 + \text{Cl}_2$

$$K_p = \frac{\frac{P}{3}\times\frac{P}{3}}{\frac{P}{3}} = \frac{P}{3} \Rightarrow P = 3K_p$$

Which of the following has minimum melting point?
questions.solution:
Ionic compounds have high melting point. Greater the ionic character, more is the melting point. HCl is a covalent molecule with least ionic character among CsF, HCl, HF and LiF (and, unlike HF, no strong hydrogen bonding).

$\therefore$ HCl has minimum melting point.

questions.stem: When $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$, $\text{CH}_4$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ pass through a test tube which has ammonical $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2$, find out which gas comes out unaffected from test tube?

$\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$ forms copper acetylide with ammonical $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2$

$\text{Cu}_2\text{Cl}_2 + 2\text{NH}_4\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{Cu}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} + 2\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$

$\text{Cu}_2\text{O} + \text{C}_2\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \underset{\text{(copper acetylide)}}{\text{Cu}_2\text{C}_2} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

Hence $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$ and $\text{CH}_4$ come out unaffected.

questions.stem: Adsorption of a gas follows Freundlich adsorption isotherm. x is the mass of the gas adsorbed on mass $m$ of the adsorbent. The plot of $\log\dfrac{x}{m}$ versus $\log p$ is shown in the given graph. $\dfrac{x}{m}$ is proportional to:
questions.solution:
According to Freundlich adsorption isotherm

$\dfrac{x}{m} = kp^{1/n} \Rightarrow \log\dfrac{x}{m} = \log k + \dfrac{1}{n}\log p$

Slope $= \dfrac{1}{n} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$\therefore \dfrac{x}{m} \propto p^{2/3}$

questions.stem: If $A + B + C = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$ then

options.text: $\tan A\tan B + \tan B\tan C + \tan C\tan A = 1$
$\cot A + \cot B + \cot C = \cot A\cot B\cot C$

questions.solution:
$\tan(A + B) = \cot C \Rightarrow \dfrac{\tan A + \tan B}{1 - \tan A\tan B} = \dfrac{1}{\tan C} \Rightarrow \sum\tan A\tan B = 1$. Dividing by $\tan A\tan B\tan C$ gives $\cot A + \cot B + \cot C = \cot A\cot B\cot C$.

Also $\cos2A + \cos2B = 2\cos(A+B)\cos(A-B) = 2\sin C\cos(A-B)$ and $\cos2C = 1 - 2\sin^2C = 1 - 2\sin C\cos(A+B)$, so the sum $= 1 + 2\sin C[\cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B)] = 1 + 4\sin A\sin B\sin C$. All three are correct.

questions.stem: The equation of the circle, which touches the line $y = 5$ and passes through $(-1, 2)$ and $(1, 2)$ is
questions.solution:
The centre of the circle is on the perpendicular bisector of the line joining $(-1, 2)$ and $(1, 2)$, which is the y-axis. The ordinate of the centre is given by

$(5 - y)^2 = 1 + (y - 2)^2 \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{10}{3}$

Hence, eq. of the circle is: $x^2 + \left(y - \dfrac{10}{3}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{5}{3}\right)^2 \Rightarrow 9x^2 + 9y^2 - 60y + 75 = 0$
$f'(x) = \dfrac{2e^{2x}(e^{2x}+1) - 2e^{2x}(e^{2x}-1)}{(e^{2x}+1)^2} = \dfrac{4e^{2x}}{(e^{2x}+1)^2} > 0$ for all $x$. Hence $f$ is an increasing function.

questions.stem: The domain of the function $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x^{12} - x^9 + x^4 - x + 1}}$ is
questions.solution:
For $x \le 0$ all terms are non-negative and the constant is 1, so the expression $> 0$. For $0 < x < 1$: $x^{12} + x^4(1 - x^5) + (1 - x) > 0$. For $x \ge 1$: $x^9(x^3 - 1) + x(x^3 - 1) + 1 > 0$.

Hence the expression is always positive and the domain is $(-\infty, \infty)$.

questions.stem: If $\displaystyle\int\frac{\sin x}{\sin(x - \alpha)}dx = Ax + B\log\sin(x - \alpha) + C$, then value of $(A, B)$ is
questions.solution:
$\sin x = \sin((x - \alpha) + \alpha) = \sin(x - \alpha)\cos\alpha + \cos(x - \alpha)\sin\alpha$

$\displaystyle\int\left[\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha\cot(x - \alpha)\right]dx = x\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha\log\sin(x - \alpha) + C$

$\therefore (A, B) = (\cos\alpha, \sin\alpha)$

questions.stem: If the sum of a certain number of terms of the A.P. $25, 22, 19, \ldots$ is $116$, then find the last term is.
questions.solution:
$S_n = \dfrac{n}{2}[50 - 3(n - 1)] = 116 \Rightarrow 3n^2 - 53n + 232 = 0 \Rightarrow (n - 8)(3n - 29) = 0 \Rightarrow n = 8$

Last term $= 25 + 7(-3) = 4$

questions.stem: If $z_1 = \sqrt{2}\left[\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right]$ and $z_2 = \sqrt{3}\left[\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right]$, then $|z_1z_2|$ is equal to $\sqrt{m}$. Value of $m$ is
questions.solution:
$z_1 = \sqrt{2}\left[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} + i\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right] = 1 + i$, $|z_1| = \sqrt{2}$

$z_2 = \sqrt{3}\left[\dfrac{1}{2} + i\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right]$, $|z_2| = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{9}{4}} = \sqrt{3}$

$|z_1z_2| = |z_1||z_2| = \sqrt{2}\cdot\sqrt{3} = \sqrt{6} \Rightarrow m = 6$

questions.stem: If the tangent at $P(1, 1)$ on $y^2 = x(2 - x)^2$ meets the curve again at $Q$, then $Q$ is
questions.solution:
$y^2 = x(2 - x)^2 \Rightarrow y^2 = x^3 - 4x^2 + 4x$ ....(i)

$\Rightarrow 2y\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 3x^2 - 8x + 4 \Rightarrow \left[\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right]_P = \dfrac{3 - 8 + 4}{2} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ Equation of tangent at P is: $y - 1 = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 1) \Rightarrow x + 2y - 3 = 0$ ....(ii)

Using $y = \dfrac{3 - x}{2}$ in (i): $\left(\dfrac{3 - x}{2}\right)^2 = x^3 - 4x^2 + 4x \Rightarrow 4x^3 - 17x^2 + 22x - 9 = 0$

which has two roots 1, 1 (because (ii) is tangent at (1, 1)). Sum of 3 roots $= \dfrac{17}{4}$, $\therefore$ 3rd root $= \dfrac{17}{4} - 2 = \dfrac{9}{4}$

Then, $y = \dfrac{3 - \frac{9}{4}}{2} = \dfrac{3}{8}$. $\therefore Q$ is $\left(\dfrac{9}{4}, \dfrac{3}{8}\right)$

questions.stem: If the harmonic mean between $a$ and $b$ be $H$, then the value of $\dfrac{1}{H - a} + \dfrac{1}{H - b}$ is
questions.solution:
Putting $H = \dfrac{2ab}{a + b}$, we have

$$\frac{1}{H - a} + \frac{1}{H - b} = \frac{a + b}{ab - a^2} + \frac{a + b}{ab - b^2} = \left(\frac{a + b}{b - a}\right)\left(\frac{1}{a} - \frac{1}{b}\right) = \left(\frac{a + b}{b - a}\right)\left(\frac{b - a}{ab}\right) = \frac{a + b}{ab} = \frac{1}{a} + \frac{1}{b}$$

questions.stem: Consider an infinite geometric series with first term $a$ and common ratio $r$. If its sum is 4 and the second term is $\dfrac{3}{4}$, then:
questions.solution:
Since sum $= 4$ and second term $= \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{a}{1 - r} = 4$, and $ar = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{a}{1 - \frac{3}{4a}} = 4 \Rightarrow (a - 1)(a - 3) = 0 \Rightarrow a = 1$ or $a = 3$

For $a = 3$, $r = \dfrac{1}{4}$.

questions.stem: The area bounded by curves $(x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1$ and $x^2 + y^2 = 1$ is
questions.solution:
Given circles are $x^2 + y^2 = 1$ ...(i) and $(x - 1)^2 + y^2 = 1$ ...(ii)

Both circles are symmetrical about x-axis. Solving (i) and (ii), we get $-2x + 1 = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{1}{2}$, then $y^2 = 1 - \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{3}{4} \Rightarrow y = \pm\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

The points of intersection are $P\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$ and $Q\left(\dfrac{1}{2}, -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)$.

Required area $= 2\times$ area of the region OLAP $= 2\left[\displaystyle\int_0^{1/2}\sqrt{1 - (x - 1)^2}\,dx + \int_{1/2}^1\sqrt{1 - x^2}\,dx\right]$

$$= 2\left[\frac{(x-1)\sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}(x-1)\right]_0^{1/2} + 2\left[\frac{x\sqrt{1-x^2}}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}x\right]_{1/2}^1 = \left(\frac{2\pi}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\ \text{sq. units}$$

questions.stem: Evaluate: $\displaystyle\int_0^\pi\frac{1}{5 + 4\cos x}dx$
questions.solution:
$$\int_0^\pi\frac{1}{5 + 4\left(\frac{1 - \tan^2\frac{x}{2}}{1 + \tan^2\frac{x}{2}}\right)}dx = \int_0^\pi\frac{1 + \tan^2\frac{x}{2}}{9 + \tan^2\frac{x}{2}}dx = \int_0^\pi\frac{\sec^2\frac{x}{2}}{9 + \tan^2\frac{x}{2}}dx$$

Let $\tan\dfrac{x}{2} = t \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\dfrac{x}{2}dx = dt$. Also, $x = 0 \Rightarrow t = 0$ and $x = \pi \Rightarrow t = \infty$

$$\therefore I = 2\int_0^\infty\frac{dt}{9 + t^2} = \frac{2}{3}\left[\tan^{-1}\frac{t}{3}\right]_0^\infty = \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - 0\right) = \frac{\pi}{3}$$

questions.stem: The points at which the tangent passes through the origin for the curve $y = 4x^3 - 2x^5$ are
questions.solution:
$y = 4x^3 - 2x^5 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 12x^2 - 10x^4$

The equation of the tangent at $(x, y)$: $Y - y = (12x^2 - 10x^4)(X - x)$ ...(i)

When the tangent passes through the origin, $X = Y = 0$: $-y = (12x^2 - 10x^4)(-x) \Rightarrow y = 12x^3 - 10x^5$

Also $y = 4x^3 - 2x^5$, $\therefore 12x^3 - 10x^5 = 4x^3 - 2x^5 \Rightarrow 8x^5 - 8x^3 = 0 \Rightarrow x^3(x^2 - 1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = 0, \pm1$

When $x = 0$, $y = 0$; when $x = 1$, $y = 2$; when $x = -1$, $y = -2$.

Hence, the required points are $(0, 0), (1, 2)$ and $(-1, -2)$.

questions.stem: The length of the perpendicular drawn from the point $(3, -1, 11)$ to the line $\dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{y - 2}{3} = \dfrac{z - 3}{4}$ is:
questions.solution:
Let foot of perpendicular be $(2\alpha, 3\alpha + 2, 4\alpha + 3)$.

Direction ratios of the perpendicular line: $2\alpha - 3, 3\alpha + 3, 4\alpha - 8$; direction ratios of the line are $2, 3, 4$.

$\Rightarrow 2(2\alpha - 3) + 3(3\alpha + 3) + 4(4\alpha - 8) = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha = 1$

$\Rightarrow$ Foot of perpendicular is $(2, 5, 7)$

$\Rightarrow$ Length $= \sqrt{1^2 + 6^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{53}$

questions.stem: Find the value of $a$ such that the sum of the squares of the roots of the equation $x^2 - (a - 2)x - (a + 1) = 0$ is least.
questions.solution:
Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots. $\alpha + \beta = a - 2$ and $\alpha\beta = -(a + 1)$

$\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha + \beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta = (a - 2)^2 + 2(a + 1) = (a - 1)^2 + 5$

$\therefore \alpha^2 + \beta^2$ will be minimum if $(a - 1)^2 = 0$, i.e. $a = 1$.

questions.stem: How many numbers lying between 999 and 10000 can be formed with the help of the digits $0, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8$, when the digits are not repeated?
questions.solution:
The numbers between 999 and 10000 are all 4-digit numbers. The number of 4-digit arrangements of the digits $0, 2, 3, 6, 7, 8$ is $^6P_4 = 360$.

Those beginning with 0 must be excluded: with initial digit 0, the remaining 3 places can be filled from five digits in $^5P_3 = 60$ ways.

So, the required numbers $= 360 - 60 = 300$.

questions.solution:
$\angle F'BF = 90^\circ$, $F'B \perp FB$, i.e. slope of $(F'B)\times$ slope of $(FB) = -1$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{b}{ae}\times\dfrac{b}{-ae} = -1 \Rightarrow b^2 = a^2e^2$

Also $b^2 = a^2(1 - e^2) \Rightarrow e^2 = 1 - e^2 \Rightarrow e = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
